biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Red Panda, Asian Elephant, Citrus indica (wild orange)

biosphereReserves.name: Manas
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Golden Langur, Pygmy Hog, Hispid Hare

biosphereReserves.name: Dibru-Saikhowa
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: White-winged Wood Duck, Feral Horses (smallest BR in India, 765 sq km)

biosphereReserves.name: Khangchendzonga
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Snow Leopard, Red Panda, Tibetan Sheep

biosphereReserves.name: Agasthyamalai
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Nilgiri Tahr, Asian Elephant, Kani tribe medicinal plants

biosphereReserves.name: Great Rann of Kutch
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Indian Wild Ass (Khur), Greater Flamingo (largest BR in India, 12,454 sq km)

biosphereReserves.name: Cold Desert
biosphereReserves.keySpecies: Snow Leopard, Tibetan Gazelle, Woolly Hare

biosphereReserves.name: Panna

mabSummary: 12 of the 18 Biosphere Reserves in India are inscribed on UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR) under the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) programme.

ramsarWetlandsSummary.leadingState: Tamil Nadu leads with 18 Ramsar sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10 sites.

keySites.name: Chilika Lake
keySites.feature: First Ramsar Site of India (designated 1981 alongside Keoladeo NP); largest coastal lagoon

keySites.name: Keoladeo National Park
keySites.feature: Montreux Record site due to ecological changes; wintering ground for migratory Siberian Cranes

keySites.name: Loktak Lake
keySites.feature: Montreux Record site; famous for floating Phumdis and Keibul Lamjao NP (Sangai brow-antlered deer)

keySites.name: Renuka Wetland
keySites.feature: Smallest Ramsar Site in India (area ~0.2 sq km)

tigerReservesSummary.topStates: Madhya Pradesh (7 reserves — Tiger State of India with 785 tigers in 2022 Census), Karnataka (5 reserves with 563 tigers), Uttarakhand (Corbett holds highest tiger density in world).
